Title: AZ BL COLO 7528(1) Burro Creek Road
Description: PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Burro Creek Road is located in Mohave County, 71 miles southwest of Kingman, Arizona. The project is located in rolling terrain, with elevations along this section ranging from approximately 1,885 to 2,255 feet. The project begins at the bridge over Burro Creek and ends at the cattle guard near the intersection with US Hwy 93. The project's length is approximately 1.3 miles. SCOPE OF THE WORK: The proposed of this resurfacing, restoration, and rehabilitation (3R) project is to improve access to the camping and day use areas at the Burro Creek Campground, reduce maintenance costs and erosion, improve sediment control, drainage and safety. The scope of work for this project includes the following major construction activities and items: Pavement Rehabilitation: 1.3 miles of roadway resurfacing incorporating Full Depth Reclamation (FDR) and Asphalt Concrete Pavement, along with applicable fog seals and tack coats. Drainage Improvements: Installation of cross culverts and reconstruction of an existing headwall. Additional drainage work includes ditch grading and reconditioning, berms, bank stabilization, and the addition of flared end sections and riprap aprons throughout the project. Earthwork & Stabilization: Embankment benching, slope stabilization, slope scaling, and specific bridge approach repairs at the eastern abutment to resolve undercutting concerns Safety & Traffic Control Items: Installation of new regulatory and warning signs, pavement markings and the placement of boulders to control public access at specific locations throughout the project. The project is structured with a base Schedule A encompassing the primary roadway rehabilitation, and an Option X which includes work associated with repairing bridge sedimentation, addressing undercutting at the bridge approaches, and boulder placement. PRINCIPAL WORK ITEMS: Roadway Aggregate: 1,600 TONS Ditch Reconditioning: 2,000 LNFT Full Depth Reclamation: 1.3 MILE Asphalt Concrete Pavement: 3,600 TON 18-Inch Pipe Culvert: 100 LNFT 24-Inch Pipe Culvert: 175 LNFT Boulder: 100 EACH ANTICIPATED SCHEDULE: Advertisement – October 2026 Award-January - 2027 Construction – January 2027 through October 2027 ESTIMATED COST RANGE: Between $2,000,000 and $5,000,000

Title: MACH1_AOI_FA890327M1006_F-47 Future Campus at Nellis AFB
Description: **Update 12 Nov 2026**: Added Attachment Q&A (Final Round) **Update 5 Nov 2026**: Added Attachment Q&A (First Round) **Update 1 Nov 2026**: Added Attachment F, Proposed Construction Markups and Commercial Pricing Perameters MACH1 Area of Interest: F-47 Future Campus at Nellis AFB, Rapid Delivery Progressive Design-Build The 772d Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS), in coordination with the Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC), is seeking highly qualified Design-Build teams to deliver the Rapid Delivery Projects supporting the F-47 mission at Nellis Air Force Base, Nevada, utilizing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) model. This Area of Interest (AOI) is issued under the Modernized Agile Construction Horizons (MACH1) Umbrella Program Notice, FA8903-OT-MACH1. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 2808a. Respondents shall comply with the MACH1 Umbrella Program Notice and the project-specific requirements established in the attached AOI. Program Overview The F-47 Campus at Nellis AFB is an approximately $1.057 billion total programmed military construction initiative intended to provide the facilities and infrastructure necessary to support the F-47 mission. This amount includes construction, contingency, design, construction security, and other applicable project costs and does not represent the construction agreement value available under this AOI. The present acquisition contemplates award for the Rapid Delivery Projects under Milestones 2 through 4 only, consisting of: Combined Operations and Maintenance Hangar. Reprogramming Laboratory. Simulator Facility. Aircraft Apron with Sunshades. Supporting utilities and infrastructure necessary for permanent operation of the Rapid Delivery facilities. The Government strongly prefers to select one Design-Build team capable of delivering all Rapid Delivery Projects, while reserving the right to select up to four teams if warranted by program requirements and permitted by the applicable acquisition authority. The Government also values organizations possessing the qualifications and resources to support the remaining Nellis F-47 Campus. However, selection under this AOI does not guarantee Milestone 5 or subsequent Agreement(s). Progressive Design-Build Delivery Approach The Government intends to initiate design and preconstruction services following completion of the Planning Charrette Reports establishing the initial mission requirements. The selected Design-Build team will work collaboratively with AFCEC and its Owner's Advisor to advance facility designs, evaluate alternative technical and construction solutions, develop cost and schedule strategies, and establish commercially supportable construction pricing. The Government contemplates negotiating firm-fixed-price construction agreement at approximately 65% design completion, subject to sufficient scope maturity, risk allocation, and commercial cost viability. Advanced design packages, early construction activities, and long-lead procurement may be considered where appropriately justified and authorized. AFCEC seeks a collaborative construction partner committed to delivering the greatest possible mission capability and value for the resources invested. The Government intends to consider innovative design and construction approaches, including industrialized construction methods, commercially effective Agreement commitment strategies, and practical alternatives that improve affordability and schedule performance. Three-Phase Selection Process The Government intends to conduct an expedited three-phase selection process under MACH1: Phase 1: Solution Brief. Respondents will submit qualifications and technical information demonstrating the capabilities of their actual proposed design and construction organizations. The attached AOI establishes ten project-specific technical factors and a maximum of 20 narrative pages, with separately permitted appendices. No construction price or rough-order-of-magnitude construction estimate is required during Phase 1 Submissions. Phase 2: Oral Presentations / Pitch Sessions. Selected respondents will be invited to participate in oral presentations. Detailed instructions and additional technical information will be provided to invited respondents, subject to applicable information-security requirements. Phase 3: Full Phase 3 Submission and Negotiations. The Government intends to conduct direct negotiations with selected respondent(s), subject to applicable authority and Agreements Officer approval. Commercial viability of the price will be evaluated before award. Anticipated Acquisition Schedule AOI Release: October 30, 2026. Initial Industry Questions Due: November 4, 2026. Final Industry Questions Due: November 10, 2026. Phase 1 Solution Briefs Due: November 18, 2026, at 9:00 PM Central Standard Time. Phase 2 Invitations: By December 2, 2026. Phase 2 Oral Presentations: December 14–17, 2026. Phase 3 Invitations: December 22, 2026. Phase 3 Submissions Due: January 15, 2027. Target Initial OTA Award: February 5, 2027. All dates are anticipated and subject to revision by the Agreements Officer. Submission Instructions Respondents shall review the complete attached AOI and MACH1 Umbrella Program Notice for eligibility requirements, technical factors, page limits, qualification-sheet requirements, cybersecurity provisions, and evaluation procedures. Phase 1 submissions shall be unclassified and submitted as a single searchable PDF with the required bookmarks and appendices. Submit Solution Briefs electronically to: 772ESS.PKA.MACH1@us.af.mil Reference the assigned Nellis F-47 Campus AOI Notice ID in the email subject line. All questions and acquisition communications shall be directed to the Agreements Officer through the designated MACH1 correspondence address. Only authorized Government officials may modify AOI requirements or make commitments binding upon the Government. The Government reserves the right to amend or cancel this AOI, request supplemental information, limit the number of respondents advancing to subsequent phases, or make no award, consistent with applicable authority. The attached AOI establishes the controlling project-specific submission requirements and evaluation procedures.

Title: 30 RS Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST)
Description: This requirement is for procurement of services including providing personnel, services, and management support for the Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST) software. The service will provide timely remote and periodic on-site support to the 30RS for MPST. The service includes maintaining compatibility with upgrades to the RQ-170 Mission Planning System (MPS) software, hardware, and databases by utilizing improved and/or expanded intelligence products. It will also ensure the software accurately represents new and/or improved aircraft capabilities, correct errors and address limitations encountered during operational use. Provide software and database maintenance and support functions to the 30 RS for the Mission Planning Support Tools (MPST) and Advanced Framework for Simulation, Integration and Modeling (AFSIM). The contractor shall provide software programming support for MPST computer program and its integration with AFSIM. All individuals performing on-site on this PWS must have a current adjudicated background investigation and be eligible for access to Top Secret, SCI, SAP information and associated ACCMs. Contractor personnel shall be conversant in the computer programming skills to fully support MPST, the version of AFSIM used by the RQ-170 simulator, be familiar with RQ-170 aircraft survivability, capabilities, Blue/Gray/Red ground and airborne threat systems, and Suppressor modeling capabilities/architecture/function/programming. Suppressor model may contain Foreign Government Information. The contractor shall provide support in training in the use of the version of AFSIM currently being used by the RQ-170. Actual work performance location is the contractor facility with periodic on-site visits to Creech AFB, NV and other classified locations as determined by the government.

Description: This intent of this project is to construct approximately 0.5 miles of barbwire fence lines near Kalamazoo Campground on the Ely Ranger District. Title: MACH1_AOI_FA890327M1006_F-47 Future Campus at Nellis AFB
Description: **Update 5 Nov 2026**: Added First Round Q&A Matrix **Update 1 Nov 2026**: Added Attachment F, Proposed Construction Markups and Commercial Pricing Perameters MACH1 Area of Interest: F-47 Future Campus at Nellis AFB, Rapid Delivery Progressive Design-Build The 772d Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS), in coordination with the Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC), is seeking highly qualified Design-Build teams to deliver the Rapid Delivery Projects supporting the F-47 mission at Nellis Air Force Base, Nevada, utilizing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) model. This Area of Interest (AOI) is issued under the Modernized Agile Construction Horizons (MACH1) Umbrella Program Notice, FA8903-OT-MACH1. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 2808a. Respondents shall comply with the MACH1 Umbrella Program Notice and the project-specific requirements established in the attached AOI. Program Overview The F-47 Campus at Nellis AFB is an approximately $1.057 billion total programmed military construction initiative intended to provide the facilities and infrastructure necessary to support the F-47 mission. This amount includes construction, contingency, design, construction security, and other applicable project costs and does not represent the construction agreement value available under this AOI. The present acquisition contemplates award for the Rapid Delivery Projects under Milestones 2 through 4 only, consisting of: Combined Operations and Maintenance Hangar. Reprogramming Laboratory. Simulator Facility. Aircraft Apron with Sunshades. Supporting utilities and infrastructure necessary for permanent operation of the Rapid Delivery facilities. The Government strongly prefers to select one Design-Build team capable of delivering all Rapid Delivery Projects, while reserving the right to select up to four teams if warranted by program requirements and permitted by the applicable acquisition authority. The Government also values organizations possessing the qualifications and resources to support the remaining Nellis F-47 Campus. However, selection under this AOI does not guarantee Milestone 5 or subsequent Agreement(s). Progressive Design-Build Delivery Approach The Government intends to initiate design and preconstruction services following completion of the Planning Charrette Reports establishing the initial mission requirements. The selected Design-Build team will work collaboratively with AFCEC and its Owner's Advisor to advance facility designs, evaluate alternative technical and construction solutions, develop cost and schedule strategies, and establish commercially supportable construction pricing. The Government contemplates negotiating firm-fixed-price construction agreement at approximately 65% design completion, subject to sufficient scope maturity, risk allocation, and commercial cost viability. Advanced design packages, early construction activities, and long-lead procurement may be considered where appropriately justified and authorized. AFCEC seeks a collaborative construction partner committed to delivering the greatest possible mission capability and value for the resources invested. The Government intends to consider innovative design and construction approaches, including industrialized construction methods, commercially effective Agreement commitment strategies, and practical alternatives that improve affordability and schedule performance. Three-Phase Selection Process The Government intends to conduct an expedited three-phase selection process under MACH1: Phase 1: Solution Brief. Respondents will submit qualifications and technical information demonstrating the capabilities of their actual proposed design and construction organizations. The attached AOI establishes ten project-specific technical factors and a maximum of 20 narrative pages, with separately permitted appendices. No construction price or rough-order-of-magnitude construction estimate is required during Phase 1 Submissions. Phase 2: Oral Presentations / Pitch Sessions. Selected respondents will be invited to participate in oral presentations. Detailed instructions and additional technical information will be provided to invited respondents, subject to applicable information-security requirements. Phase 3: Full Phase 3 Submission and Negotiations. The Government intends to conduct direct negotiations with selected respondent(s), subject to applicable authority and Agreements Officer approval. Commercial viability of the price will be evaluated before award. Anticipated Acquisition Schedule AOI Release: October 30, 2026. Initial Industry Questions Due: November 4, 2026. Final Industry Questions Due: November 10, 2026. Phase 1 Solution Briefs Due: November 18, 2026, at 9:00 PM Central Standard Time. Phase 2 Invitations: By December 2, 2026. Phase 2 Oral Presentations: December 14–17, 2026. Phase 3 Invitations: December 22, 2026. Phase 3 Submissions Due: January 15, 2027. Target Initial OTA Award: February 5, 2027. All dates are anticipated and subject to revision by the Agreements Officer. Submission Instructions Respondents shall review the complete attached AOI and MACH1 Umbrella Program Notice for eligibility requirements, technical factors, page limits, qualification-sheet requirements, cybersecurity provisions, and evaluation procedures. Phase 1 submissions shall be unclassified and submitted as a single searchable PDF with the required bookmarks and appendices. Submit Solution Briefs electronically to: 772ESS.PKA.MACH1@us.af.mil Reference the assigned Nellis F-47 Campus AOI Notice ID in the email subject line. All questions and acquisition communications shall be directed to the Agreements Officer through the designated MACH1 correspondence address. Only authorized Government officials may modify AOI requirements or make commitments binding upon the Government. The Government reserves the right to amend or cancel this AOI, request supplemental information, limit the number of respondents advancing to subsequent phases, or make no award, consistent with applicable authority. The attached AOI establishes the controlling project-specific submission requirements and evaluation procedures.

Description: VA Northern California Health Care System 612A4-27-018 Page 4 of 5 Statement of Work Replace B650 3rd and 2nd Flooring Project #612A4-27-018 General Intention: The purpose of this project is to replace flooring, resilient base, stainless steel corner guards, and paint throughout B650 3rd and 2nd Floor of the Sacramento Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC) of VA Northern California Healthcare System (VANCHCS). Contractor shall furnish all labor and materials needed to perform all demolition, replacement, and installation required by this scope as required by specifications. Visits to the site by bidders may be made only by appointment with the Contracting Officer (CO) for the project. A preliminary/pre-proposal site visit is strongly encouraged and shall be coordinated with the Contracting Officer Representative (COR). Location of work; the geographic location for service(s) are the following areas: Sacramento VA Medical Center 10535 Hospital Way Mather, CA 95655 Buildings: 650 3rd and 2nd Floors The contractor shall consider that there are no staging areas available within the facility premises. If necessary, staging areas may be put into effect at the discretion of the COR, depending on availability. The Contractor shall note that there is absolutely NO Contractor employee parking in Patient Parking designated areas. VANCHCS will not invalidate or make reimbursement for parking violations for the Contractor under any conditions. The contractor will be responsible for disposing of all equipment components and trash demolished or replaced as part of this project. The contractor is responsible for following infection control procedures per VA specifications and site infection control protocols. Schedule of work: All work shall be performed outside of normal working hours, which are 7:30 AM to 4:00 PM, Monday through Friday, excluding weekends and holidays unless approved by the CO. Work during normal hours may only be scheduled if it is planned at least three weeks in advance for a specific location and approved by the appropriate VA personnel. Any work activities that generate noise or disruption sufficient to impact patient care, disturb patients, or interfere with staff operations must be conducted only after normal working hours or on weekends. The contractor is responsible for coordinating with VA COR to ensure all work scheduling complies with this requirement and must provide notification of planned work at least three weeks prior to commencement. Emergency work or exceptions to this schedule must be requested in writing and approved by the CO. The Contractor shall prepare any necessary construction documents and provide all necessary/required professional engineering services to include, but not limited to tools, equipment, materials, labor, travel, expertise, supervision, testing, analysis, and specialty services to accomplish all items and requirements outlined in this SOW. All work shall comply with all applicable federal, state, local and VA regulations and requirements. Scope of Work: The contractor shall replace approximately 38,000 square feet (SF) of carpet and luxury vinyl tile throughout Building 650 3rd and 2nd Floors as shown in Exhibit A - BLDG 650 2nd and 3rd Floors Room Flooring Replacement and Attachment 1 - BLDG 650 Mather 2nd and 3rd Floor Carpet Replacement Current Flooring. Resilient wall base shall also be replaced at all spaces that will receive new flooring. The Contractor shall refer to Specification Section 09 06 00, Schedules for Finishes, for the products and finishes required under this contract. Title: MACH1_AOI_FA890327M1006_F-47 Future Campus at Nellis AFB
Description: **Update 1 Nov 2026**: Added Attachment F, Proposed Construction Markups and Commercial Pricing Perameters MACH1 Area of Interest: F-47 Future Campus at Nellis AFB, Rapid Delivery Progressive Design-Build The 772d Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS), in coordination with the Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC), is seeking highly qualified Design-Build teams to deliver the Rapid Delivery Projects supporting the F-47 mission at Nellis Air Force Base, Nevada, utilizing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) model. This Area of Interest (AOI) is issued under the Modernized Agile Construction Horizons (MACH1) Umbrella Program Notice, FA8903-OT-MACH1. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 2808a. Respondents shall comply with the MACH1 Umbrella Program Notice and the project-specific requirements established in the attached AOI. Program Overview The F-47 Campus at Nellis AFB is an approximately $1.057 billion total programmed military construction initiative intended to provide the facilities and infrastructure necessary to support the F-47 mission. This amount includes construction, contingency, design, construction security, and other applicable project costs and does not represent the construction agreement value available under this AOI. The present acquisition contemplates award for the Rapid Delivery Projects under Milestones 2 through 4 only, consisting of: Combined Operations and Maintenance Hangar. Reprogramming Laboratory. Simulator Facility. Aircraft Apron with Sunshades. Supporting utilities and infrastructure necessary for permanent operation of the Rapid Delivery facilities. The Government strongly prefers to select one Design-Build team capable of delivering all Rapid Delivery Projects, while reserving the right to select up to four teams if warranted by program requirements and permitted by the applicable acquisition authority. The Government also values organizations possessing the qualifications and resources to support the remaining Nellis F-47 Campus. However, selection under this AOI does not guarantee Milestone 5 or subsequent Agreement(s). Progressive Design-Build Delivery Approach The Government intends to initiate design and preconstruction services following completion of the Planning Charrette Reports establishing the initial mission requirements. The selected Design-Build team will work collaboratively with AFCEC and its Owner's Advisor to advance facility designs, evaluate alternative technical and construction solutions, develop cost and schedule strategies, and establish commercially supportable construction pricing. The Government contemplates negotiating firm-fixed-price construction agreement at approximately 65% design completion, subject to sufficient scope maturity, risk allocation, and commercial cost viability. Advanced design packages, early construction activities, and long-lead procurement may be considered where appropriately justified and authorized. AFCEC seeks a collaborative construction partner committed to delivering the greatest possible mission capability and value for the resources invested. The Government intends to consider innovative design and construction approaches, including industrialized construction methods, commercially effective Agreement commitment strategies, and practical alternatives that improve affordability and schedule performance. Three-Phase Selection Process The Government intends to conduct an expedited three-phase selection process under MACH1: Phase 1: Solution Brief. Respondents will submit qualifications and technical information demonstrating the capabilities of their actual proposed design and construction organizations. The attached AOI establishes ten project-specific technical factors and a maximum of 20 narrative pages, with separately permitted appendices. No construction price or rough-order-of-magnitude construction estimate is required during Phase 1 Submissions. Phase 2: Oral Presentations / Pitch Sessions. Selected respondents will be invited to participate in oral presentations. Detailed instructions and additional technical information will be provided to invited respondents, subject to applicable information-security requirements. Phase 3: Full Phase 3 Submission and Negotiations. The Government intends to conduct direct negotiations with selected respondent(s), subject to applicable authority and Agreements Officer approval. Commercial viability of the price will be evaluated before award. Anticipated Acquisition Schedule AOI Release: October 30, 2026. Initial Industry Questions Due: November 4, 2026. Final Industry Questions Due: November 10, 2026. Phase 1 Solution Briefs Due: November 18, 2026, at 9:00 PM Central Standard Time. Phase 2 Invitations: By December 2, 2026. Phase 2 Oral Presentations: December 14–17, 2026. Phase 3 Invitations: December 22, 2026. Phase 3 Submissions Due: January 15, 2027. Target Initial OTA Award: February 5, 2027. All dates are anticipated and subject to revision by the Agreements Officer. Submission Instructions Respondents shall review the complete attached AOI and MACH1 Umbrella Program Notice for eligibility requirements, technical factors, page limits, qualification-sheet requirements, cybersecurity provisions, and evaluation procedures. Phase 1 submissions shall be unclassified and submitted as a single searchable PDF with the required bookmarks and appendices. Submit Solution Briefs electronically to: 772ESS.PKA.MACH1@us.af.mil Reference the assigned Nellis F-47 Campus AOI Notice ID in the email subject line. All questions and acquisition communications shall be directed to the Agreements Officer through the designated MACH1 correspondence address. Only authorized Government officials may modify AOI requirements or make commitments binding upon the Government. The Government reserves the right to amend or cancel this AOI, request supplemental information, limit the number of respondents advancing to subsequent phases, or make no award, consistent with applicable authority. The attached AOI establishes the controlling project-specific submission requirements and evaluation procedures.
